newsitem.title: UK: International tourism seen growing through yr 2000.
newsitem.headline: International tourism seen growing through yr 2000.

text.p: International tourism is expected to be a strong growth industry through the end of this century, with increases in disposable income encouraging more Asians to travel abroad, according to a report released on Wednesday.

"The industry has generally performed well over the last six years, despite a downturn in 1993 due to worldwide recession, and is forecast to continue growing to 2000," Euromonitor, a market research firm, said in its report World Tourism.

Tourism arrivals are expected to grow about four to five percent a year through the year 2000, underpinned by increased leisure time, higher disposable incomes and economic improvement, Euromonitor said. The number of international arrivals during the period 1991 to 1996 rose 27 percent to 592 million.
International tourism receipts grew 49 percent to $404 billion from 1991 to 1996.

Asia is seen as having the greatest potential for growth in tourism. "The cutting of the working week in China from 48 hours to 40 hours and the return of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty will encourage growth of outbound and domestic tourism in the country," Euromonitor said.

France continues to be the world's leading tourist destination, luring 62 million international tourists in 1996, Euromonitor said. More than half of Europe's 15 most popular tourist attractions are in France, led by Disneyland Paris. Paris attracts about 20 million tourists a year, Euromonitor said.
Europe is the world's largest tourism market, attracting 59 percent of tourists in 1996.

The Americas are the second most popular tourist destination, with South America and the Caribbean both growth markets. The world's fastest-growing tourism regions are North and Southeast Asia, Australasia and the Middle East, Euromonitor said.
